hints.title: Shortest Distance via Breadth-First Search
hints.text: Use breadth-first search from the start coordinate to compute the shortest walking distance to each cell.

hints.title: Filter by Price Range
hints.text: Whenever a cell contains an item with price within the specified range [low, high], collect its distance, price, row, and column.

hints.title: Rank by Tie-Breaking Rules
hints.text: Sort the collected candidates by distance, then price, then row, then column, and select the top k.

hints.title: Complete Python Solution
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def highestRankedKItems(self, grid: List[List[int]], pricing: List[int], start: List[int], k: int) -> List[List[int]]:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        low, high = pricing
        sr, sc = start
        q = collections.deque([(sr, sc, 0)])
        visited = [[False] * n for _ in range(m)]
        visited[sr][sc] = True
        items = []
        if low <= grid[sr][sc] <= high:
            items.append((0, grid[sr][sc], sr, sc))
        
        while q:
            r, c, d = q.popleft()
            for dr, dc in [(-1,0), (1,0), (0,-1), (0,1)]:
                nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                if 0 <= nr < m and 0 <= nc < n and not visited[nr][nc] and grid[nr][nc] != 0:
                    visited[nr][nc] = True
                    q.append((nr, nc, d + 1))
                    if low <= grid[nr][nc] <= high:
                        items.append((d + 1, grid[nr][nc], nr, nc))
        items.sort()
        return [[r, c] for _, _, r, c in items[:k]]
```

complexity.time: O(N) single pass or optimal algorithmic traversal
variables: N: input size or row count
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching paths individually from every priced item creates redundant traversals.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Single BFS across M*N cells runs in O(M*N log(M*N)) time for sorting and O(M*N) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Traverse unweighted grid with BFS to ensure optimal distances naturally.
